audit_scope: Native constructor unchanged. Query inputs and demo answers only reach independent uniqueness gate. No majority, palette or scan-order tie breaking. 250 episodes, 1000 fresh pairs, all eight D4 and shared random palette.
provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.author: host parallel coverage worker
draft_notes.explanation: Scan every visible 3x3 neighbourhood. Its eight neighbours must share one non-background colour, and its non-background centre must differ. Return the sole distinct centre colour across all qualifying windows. Multiple frames are retained when their centre colours agree. The direct target uses NumPy shifted arrays; the independent gate enumerates perimeter coordinate sets. Every demonstration must agree, and each query must have one visible answer. No query output is read by the gate.
draft_notes.limitations: Native scatter can rarely form a second ring with a different centre colour. The constructor is unchanged and still generates that full domain. Such ambiguous scenes are explicitly rejected based on visible input, rather than using hidden planting position, palette ordering, majority vote or scan order. Same-colour duplicate frames and touching scatter remain admissible. Background is specialised to palette[0], not estimated by frequency.

host_review.reason: Replace unsupported majority/lower-colour fallback and reject proposed constructor narrowing. Preserve explicit ambiguous counterexample as evidence of unavoidable output uncertainty.
